nh_rumney_bouldering.blurb: Rumney Bouldering lies on the hillside around Rumney, a town far better known for its sport cliffs. The boulders are tucked among trees, and new problems are cleaned and climbed every season. Nearly all the problems are bouldering, with a sprinkle of trad and top-rope. The Black Jack Boulders hold the great majority, with smaller groups near the main parking meadows, along the Short Cut Trail and along the Pink Flag Trail. Grades start at V0 and are well spread from V0 through V7, thinning out toward V13. Moderate and mid-grade problems are plentiful.

ut_san_rafael_swell_south.blurb: San Rafael Swell - South is a huge, sparsely visited stretch of central Utah south of I-70 and west of Green River. The San Rafael Reef is a steep ridge tilting east, and its big sandstone slabs, plus isolated towers and domes, make this an adventure-climbing area. Trad dominates, with long multi-pitch routes, some of five to nine pitches, and a small amount of sport, aid and bouldering. Grades run from easy scrambling terrain to 5.12, with most climbs between 5.8 and 5.10. The Eastern Reef holds most routes, with Upper Muddy Creek, Viewfinder Towers and Family Butte scattered farther out. Services are far away, old roads criss-cross the desert and you will see few other parties, so carry maps.

ga_rocktown.blurb: Rocktown is a dense field of sandstone boulders on top of Pigeon Mountain in northwest Georgia, near LaFayette. The boulders cover several acres and average around 30 to 40 feet tall. It is almost all bouldering, from V0 up to about V11, with most problems between V2 and V8. The elevation brings a breeze, which makes spring a prime time, while summer humidity makes friction harder. Sections differ in feel: Hueco Simulator in the upper maze has easy, jug-heavy problems and plenty of sun, while a boulder in the lower maze stays shaded. The Asphalt area has easy to moderate problems and a few harder lines.

sd_iron_mountain.blurb: Iron Mountain is a Black Hills area near Mount Rushmore, at about 4,800 feet. Granite bouldering is the main draw, a big cluster of problems with highballs among them and some schist in places. Short face routes on trad and sport lines sit alongside, and there is enough bouldering to leave the rope at home. Boulder grades run from V0 to V11, mostly in the easy to mid range, while roped climbs mostly span 5.9 to 5.12. Raspberry Rocks, Turtle Dome and the area near the first pigtail bridge hold the most climbs. Turtle Dome offers lots of moderates on granite and schist. It is quieter than the busier Black Hills spots.

ar_cowell_deer_area.blurb: Cowell/Deer is a backwoods sandstone area in the Ozarks of north-central Arkansas, reached from Highway 7 south of Jasper. It is split between sport climbing and bouldering, with a little trad. Sport routes cluster in the 5.10 to 5.13 range, with the biggest share around 5.11 and 5.12, while boulder problems are spread from V0 into the V13 range. Cowell holds most of it, with steep walls offering powerful problems and sport lines, plus a main bouldering area. Haunt Hollow is a smaller sport crag with roughly two dozen to thirty lines. The area is still fairly quiet and spread out through the woods.

ca_rock_creek.blurb: Rock Creek is a granite canyon in the Eastern Sierra between Bishop and Mammoth Lakes, reached by the road from Tom's Place, with formations on the canyon's west side. The elevation is about 7,500 feet, and snowfall makes it mainly a summer area. Trad makes up most of it, with a solid portion of sport and a small bouldering sector. Roped grades run from 5.7 to 5.13, concentrated around 5.10, with another large group in the 5.9 and 5.11 range. Gong Show Wall and Patricia Bowl hold the most routes, with Juniper Wall, the 4:20 Wall and a bouldering area nearby. Mammoth climbing in general begins in late April or May and runs through November.
